sonnet.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'They're in the valley…', 'It stretches from…', and 'Friend, my whole cookie planet…'. Only the opening card may be longer than 2 sentences.
sonnet.rule: **Every other story card, including the first card of a later stop, is 1 to 2 sentences.**

sonnet.problem: The question says God speaks 'out of the fire', and the right answer is 'afraid of the fire'. The question already holds a form of the answer, and the right answer is the only one that echoes it.
sonnet.rule: A choice card's question never holds its own answer, or a form of it, like "rock badgers" for "in the rocks." Ask something else.

sonnet.problem: Card 3 already asked who must not work on the Sabbath and gave the answer that servants are included. Card 4 repeated it. Card 5 asks again that the servants get the Sabbath, so it re-asks the same fact.
sonnet.rule: An easy follow-up asks something new. It never re-asks the same fact. Two lines that make the same point get one question. An answer shown on one card, right or wrong, isn't used again on a later card.

sonnet.problem: The blank asks the baker to guess a word in the line 'false witness against their ___'. The baker has not seen the wording, and 'neighbor', 'king' and 'priest' are all plausible. It cannot be reasoned out.
sonnet.rule: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

sonnet.problem: The card spends its words explaining the hard word 'covet' ('isn't about doing something. It's about wanting'). Hard words belong in the dictionary pop-up.
sonnet.rule: **Don't spend card words explaining a hard word.** Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).

sonnet.problem: The question says 'out of the fire' (card 5 and the setup), and the right answer is 'The great fire will consume them'. The question holds a form of the answer, and the right answer is the only one that shares the word.
sonnet.rule: A choice card's question never holds its own answer, or a form of it, like "rock badgers" for "in the rocks." Ask something else.

sonnet.problem: The card says the LORD heard 'every word' the people spoke. Verse 28 says only 'the LORD heard the words you spoke', and 'every' stretches the text. This is narration, not one of Papa Dorin's own jokes.
sonnet.rule: **Don't stretch the text.** Exaggerate only in his own jokes.
